latin: Propositio dicens quod sensibile supra sensum positum non facit sensationem, non est uera nisi per accidens.
latin_note: 1486 read 'dicens que sensibile', emended in the Emendationes errorum to 'dicens quod sensibile' and so adopted by 1487 (farmer1998:13691); the sheet already gives the emended reading.
translation: That a sensible object set directly against the sense organ produces no sensation is a claim true only per accidens.
